newsitem.title: BURMA: Burmas' SLORC unswayed by U.S. sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Burmas' SLORC unswayed by U.S. sanctions.

text.p: One of Burma's military leaders said on Tuesday his government would not be swayed by U.S. economic sanctions against his country and denied Western allegations of human rights abuses. "It's not a problem for us," Lieutenant-General Khin Nyunt told foreign journalists accompanying a government trip to the Golden Triangle area in eastern Shan state.
The U.S. State Department was due to announce economic sanctions on Burma later on Tuesday, an administration official said in Washington. The sanctions will ban new U.S. investment in Burma.

Khin Nyunt, the powerful military intelligence chief and Secretary One of the State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC), said the U.S. move was no surprise. "In politics you have to expect such things," he said.

Asked whether Burma's military rulers would reconsider government policy because of the sanctions move, he said: "We don't have anything to reconsider because we are walking in a straight line. We have decided we will not stray (from our course)."

Khin Nyunt said U.S. and Western charges against the SLORC of human rights violations were unfounded. "Politics is played by some people in Rangoon, but in the country areas everything is running normally," he said.
